# Q1/Q2 reference source review, 2026-10-28

Read-only review of the frozen mx checkout at
`/zpool1/llmx-xdev-quant-20261020/q1-q2-20261027/mx-matched-v1/source`,
revision recorded as `c4d12e2c0094c9028318bed5bb1a30bb48f8a35b`.
llmx base: `9daba5511`, branch `feat/q1-q2-weights-20261027`.
No benchmark, runtime edit or new correctness pass in this review.

## Concrete differences

- mx Vulkan Q1 has no Q8_1 vector pipeline in the dispatch switch
  (`ggml/src/ggml-vulkan/ggml-vulkan.cpp:5531`). The missing pipeline
  resets quantize_y and selects the floating-activation kernel at 6702-6709.
  Do not describe the measured Vulkan Q1 reference as the ROCm integer path.
- On AMD GCN, rm_stdq is 2 (2883-2886); Q1/Q2 floating vector pipelines
  take 2*rm_stdq rows (2945-2946), hence four rows. In
  `vulkan-shaders/mul_mat_vec.comp:45-93`, activation vectors are loaded
  before the per-row loop, then each row is expanded and consumed.
  This supports testing our prepared four-row integer specialization after
  the measured row-local scheduling improvement. It does not prove a gain.
- mx Vulkan declines activation quantization on AMD for a single vector
  with K < 2048 (`ggml-vulkan.cpp:6580-6605`). The Q2 model's 1024-wide
  projections meet that condition. Wider products can use another path.
  Our current block-int16 path therefore differs in both activation
  representation and reduction. A narrow floating-path experiment must be
  measured and independently qualified, not treated as an arithmetic no-op.
- mx Vulkan Q2 MMVQ expands unsigned codes 0..3 and subtracts an activation
  sum correction after the integer dot (`mul_mat_vecq_funcs.glsl:37-55`,
  160-170). Its Q8_1 activation representation differs from our block-int16
  centered codes -1..2. It is not a drop-in correctness oracle.
- mx HIP Q2 centers codes to -1..2 before packed int8 dots, using AMD byte
  permutation (`ggml/src/ggml-cuda/vecdotq.cuh:728-771`). Q1 also uses
  packed int8 activations there (678-725). Our signed int16 pairing cannot
  adopt the int8 arithmetic unchanged. Decode mapping agrees with our
  `low_bits.glsl`; source review found no missing Q2 code or sign correction.

## Next bounded checks

1. Q1: build the prepared four-row integer specialization, inspect register
   usage, run affected native checks, then a matched performance screen.
   Keep per-row arithmetic and range repair unchanged. Only a winning
   screen warrants the expensive depth identity checks.
2. Q2: localize the residual Rome F16 top-five mismatch with shared-input
   layer witnesses. Reference dispatch is a clue, not evidence the mismatch
   is harmless. Main/Q4 passes the selected full-HF check while Q2 gets 4/5.
   Neither HF shape places token 41479 in its top five. No limit amendment.

The previous floating four-row trials and the rejected streamed-pair loop
remain valid negative results. This integer four-row schedule is a distinct
experiment, not a rerun concealed by a different name.
